target_customer: Latinos in Latin America (notably Venezuela) and the U.S. who want dollar-denominated savings and cheap transfers
problem: Cross-border payments to Latin America are costly and local currencies lose value, so people want to hold and send USDC.
business_model: Consumer stablecoin wallet and card with fees and spreads, plus merchant payment links and APIs

founders.name: Jesus Alberto Castillo Ferrer
previous_startups: Largest micro-lending platform in Venezuela (500k+ SMBs, per YC page)

founders.name: Gino Guatavita
previous_startups: Two fintechs built and scaled in Colombia, Mexico and Ecuador (per launch post, names not given)

technical_complexity.rationale: Wallet, on-ramps and card programs depend on partners; the hard parts are compliance and payment rails rather than novel technology.

defensibility.rationale: Local licensing in Venezuela through a SUNACRIP-licensed entity helps, but wallets and stablecoin apps are easy to replicate and partners can cut access.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; U.S. banking partners reportedly cut Kontigo off over Venezuela sanctions concerns.

market_need_then: Venezuelan inflation made dollar-denominated apps a daily need; the company reported $540k deposits, 10k active users and a 300k waitlist within 20 days of its P2P onramp launch (company claim).

branding.domain_note: Moved from kontigo.lat to kontigo.com (307 redirect observed).

identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, simple and aspirational Spanish copy such as 'El unico neobanco que necesitas'.

branding.community_and_virality: Site claims a 4.9 rating and 10,000+ reviews; unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: Coverage of the product is wide, but no source discusses the brand itself. Name resembles Spanish 'contigo' (with you) and the drinkware brand Contigo, which helps recall but invites confusion.

outcome_analysis: Kontigo grew fast from its Summer 2024 batch, reporting 1M users and over $30M annualized revenue by December 2025 when it announced a $20M seed. Founder fit with Venezuela and demand for dollar savings drove growth. Risks include sanctions scrutiny, loss of U.S. banking partners and a January 2026 security breach that was reimbursed.
notes: The press release fetch returned 403; the $20M seed dated 2025-12-19 to 22 comes from search results citing the press release and FinTech Futures. The $100M valuation is repeated by aggregators, so it is marked estimated. Lead investor conflicts (DST Global vs FoundersX); list is unattributed. Caplight Series A banner is unrelated site content. Breach figures vary: $340,905 and 1,005 users vs 1,059 accounts. Pre-batch funding from DST Global and others is stated by the company on its YC page but no round amounts were found. Competitors named by sources are dated 2025 or 2026, so the founding list is left empty. Company site now describes Kontigo as a super app, not only a neobank.
